warnings.headline: Storm Boelo bringing a very windy spell this weekend with some disruption possible across parts of Northern Ireland. : UPDATED
warnings.description: Information on update: Changes to start and end the warning earlier. Strong winds will spread across Northern Ireland during Saturday. Initially strong southerly winds will develop on Saturday morning, before stronger westerly winds follow later in the day. Very windy conditions will persist overnight and into Sunday before gradually easing from the southwest during Sunday morning. Gusts of 50-60 mph are likely widely with some coastal and exposed areas potentially seeing gusts of 65-75 mph. Strong winds will be combined with blustery heavy showers.
impacts: There is a chance that power cuts may occur, with the potential to affect other services, such as mobile phone coverage
There is a small chance of injuries and danger to life from flying debris
Some damage to buildings and trees, such as tiles blown from roofs and large branches or trees blown over, could happen
There is a small chance of longer journey times or cancellations as road, rail, air and ferry services are affected
There is a small chance that some roads and bridges could close
There is a small chance that injuries and danger to life could occur from large waves and beach material being thrown onto sea fronts, coastal roads and properties

warnings.headline: Storm Boelo will bring a very windy and wet spell this weekend with some disruption likely across parts of northern UK. : UPDATED
warnings.description: Information on update: Warning extended further south across northern England and into north Wales. . Strong winds will spread across northern parts of the UK during Saturday afternoon, combining with spells of heavy rain. Initially strong southerly winds will affect parts of Scotland before more widespread and even stronger westerly winds develop later on Saturday. Very windy conditions will then persist overnight and through much of Sunday before gradually easing from the southwest later. Gusts of 55-65 mph are likely widely with some coastal and exposed areas potentially seeing gusts of 70-80 mph or more, these strongest gusts most likely across Scotland and the far north of England.
impacts: Injuries and danger to life from flying debris are possible
Some damage to buildings and trees, such as tiles blown from roofs and large branches or trees blown over, could happen
Road, rail, air and ferry services may be affected, with longer journey times and cancellations possible
Some roads and bridges may close
Power cuts may occur, with the potential to affect other services, such as mobile phone coverage
Injuries and danger to life could occur from large waves and beach material being thrown onto sea fronts, coastal roads and properties

warnings.headline: The strongest winds from Storm Boelo are expected from Saturday evening, extending eastwards through Sunday. : UPDATED
warnings.description: Information on update: Warning extended further south across northern England, and Northern Ireland removed due to differing timings. . Very strong westerly winds associated with Storm Boelo are expected to bring fairly widespread gusts of 60 to 70 mph and gusts to 80 mph in exposed coastal areas. The strongest winds will initially affect western Scotland on Saturday evening, spreading eastwards overnight and through Sunday. High winds will be accompanied by periods of heavy rain and frequent showers. Whilst high winds are expected across a wider area with a yellow warning in force, there is a higher confidence in impacts and disruption taking place within this amber warning area. The winds will gradually ease from the southwest through Sunday.

warnings.headline: Heavy rain associated with Storm Boelo is likely to cause some travel disruption and flooding in a few places
warnings.description:
Frequent heavy showers or more organised bands of rain will develop across northern Scotland during Saturday evening in association with Storm Boelo, continuing through Sunday morning and early afternoon. 

Accumulations of 20-40 mm are expected widely within the warning area through this period, with 60-80 mm possible in some locations, bringing flooding and travel disruption in a few places. Showers will become less frequent later through Sunday afternoon.
impacts: Flooding of a few homes and businesses is possible
Bus and train services probably affected with journey times taking longer
Spray and flooding on roads probably making journey times longer

warnings.headline: A period of strong winds may lead to damaging gusts and transport disruption.
warnings.description: Strong west to southwesterly winds are expected to spread across much of Scotland, the north of Northern Ireland and northern England on Tuesday. Gusts of 50-60 mph are possible quite widely and some coastal or exposed areas could see gusts of 70 mph or more, but at this time there is some uncertainty in where, and how strong, the peak gusts will be. The strongest of the winds will reduce from the southwest later on Tuesday, with the far north of Scotland the last to see winds ease.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: Irish Sea at New Brighton
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: Irish Sea at New Brighton
warnings.description:
High tides are expected to cause flooding this evening. 

Flooding is expected from 10:45 PM 24 October 2026. 

Locations most affected will be Marine Point Leisure and Retail Park. We anticipate the next high tide tomorrow afternoon, 25 October 2026, to meet the flood alert threshold. We are expecting higher than normal high tides over the next 2 days, and a result, we may issue further flood alerts and flood warnings. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Start acting on your flood plan if you have one.   

This message will be updated by 9:30AM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.
impacts: Flooding is expected - act now

warnings.event: Flood Warning: River Barle from Simonsbath to Brushford, including Withypool
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: River Barle from Simonsbath to Brushford, including Withypool
warnings.description:
High river levels are expected to cause flooding today. 

Flooding is expected on Saturday 24 October  

Properties and low lying areas will start to flood from around 7 pm on Saturday. The main areas of concern are Simonsbath and Brushford, including Simonsbath, Withypool, Newbridge, Northmoor Road, Brushford and the B3222 and B3223 at Dulverton. Flood waters may be deep and fast flowing in these areas. 
River levels are forecast to be at their highest between 6 pm and 10 pm. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   

This message will be updated by 6:00PM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.
impacts: Flooding is expected - act now
